label: D1 reset dips sharply after a1->S2 (rare) trials, esp. unrewarded; belief in S2 raises it
terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") ;; (phase == D1) * (last_is("a2 S1 r") + last_is("a2 S1 u") + last_is("a2 S2 r") + last_is("a1 S1 r")) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (ep_trial/100)**3 ;; (phase == D1) * belief_lo ;; (phase != D1) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D2) * last_is("a1 S2 u") ;; (phase != D1) * (prev_action == 2)
explanation: Raw reset gate r of unit 38 is high (~0.9) almost always. Beyond timing, the dominant driver is the previous trial at D1: after a1 that landed in S2 (rare) the gate drops strongly, by ~0.39 if unrewarded and ~0.29 if rewarded; after a2 trials and a1 S1 rewarded trials it sits ~0.08 higher than after a1 S1 unrewarded / a2 S2 unrewarded. Unrewarded D1 steps late in the episode drop further (cubic in episode trial, w ~ -0.07), which accounts for much of the late-episode dip. A graded belief term (ideal-observer log-odds that S1 is good) lowers it when S1 is believed good and raises it when S2 is, at all phases; at D2 after a1 S2 u it stays ~0.09 lower, and GO/D2 run slightly higher after a2. Uses only observed quantities. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.685 (dev 0.698), vs all-observed reference 0.77 and all ceiling 0.84 (81% of ceiling). The earlier model-based version leaned on the policy (policy decile alone 0.57 vs belief decile 0.33), but here the previous-trial pattern carries most of it (last-trial table 0.66), so losing model outputs costs little. Future variables (this reward 0.01) do not matter.

terms: (phase == D1) * (last_is("a2 S1 r") + last_is("a2 S1 u") + last_is("a2 S2 r") + last_is("a1 S1 r"))
(phase == D1) * (last_is("a2 S1 r") + last_is("a2 S1 u") + last_is("a2 S2 r") + last_is("a1 S1 r"))

issues: Overclaim about the cubic late-episode term. The explanation says it 'accounts for much of the late-episode dip', but dropping it only moves test R^2 from 0.685 to 0.681. The late dip (D1 baseline falls from 0.865 to 0.69 in decile 9) is already in the timing baseline, so this term adds almost nothing.

The grouped '+0.08' term blurs two different effects. Scored separately on test, a2->S1 rare trials give +0.114 and a2 S2 r / a1 S1 r give +0.071. The residual table agrees: a2 S1 r +0.145 and a2 S1 u +0.131, against a1 S1 r +0.029. So rare a2->S1 raises D1 reset whether or not it was rewarded, the mirror image of the a1->S2 dip. The label only mentions the dip.
The belief claim holds. Removing both belief_lo terms drops test R^2 from 0.685 to 0.602. The belief effect also grows across the episode: scaling belief_lo by (1+ep_trial/50) adds about 0.01-0.02.

No large systematic error class remains. Misses gives mean phase errors of at most 0.005, and the worst (phase, previous trial) cell is D1 after a2 S1 r at +0.075. The worst windows are late-episode (t>90) ones, where the activation is about 0.13 at the window's first D1. There the previous trial is unknown ('?'), so last_is cannot fire, and a (phase==D1)*(prev_action==-1)*(prev_reward==0) term recovers some of that. GO/D2 are also over-predicted by about 0.2 in those windows.

The model still falls short of what observed cues allow: 0.685 against 0.77 for all observed cues. Some of the gap is D2's own observed choice: replacing (phase!=D1)*(prev_action==2) with GO prev_action plus D2 action helps a little.
